claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake (supersede) an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, once an execution is running in a stage, it is protected from being superseded (the lock only protects an execution once it is running).
With a CodePipeline pipeline in SUPERSEDED mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, a queued execution waiting behind a busy stage can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
When defining a CodePipeline pipeline, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set to use QUEUED mode.
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can be used to set a CodePipeline pipeline's `executionMode` and `pipelineType`.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works' documents the pipeline execution mode.
The Pulumi registry page /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists for the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource.
When two pipeline runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that prevents concurrent runs of a deployment job targeting that environment.
The exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab in Azure DevOps.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, a `lockBehavior` property can be set on a stage that references an environment with an exclusive lock check.
The `lockBehavior` stage property accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines stage `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.

With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older queued runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack, one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
The Pulumi@1 Azure Pipelines task accepts `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` inputs.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and documents Pulumi update conflicts.
The page /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists in the Pulumi Registry.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs reach the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default behavior is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available (no concurrency limit by default).
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the page describing update conflicts.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is `0`, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to `1` causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by the deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments.
In Azure Pipelines, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` makes runs queue for the exclusive lock in order.
The Pulumi docs contain a page at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ with a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting, and setting it to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs contain a page at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ with a section anchored 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', and setting it to 1 serializes Pulumi deployment builds.
The Pulumi docs contain a TeamCity guide at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ with a section anchored 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
